title: de.hubtask.work.attachment.added.v1
description: An entry now carries a file. Single-value enums stand in for `const`, and the bounds of a value are stated in its description rather than as keywords: the contract test validates against this file with the subset of JSON Schema the project implements, and a keyword it silently ignored would be a promise nobody checks. The wire format is a CloudEvent 1.0 in structured JSON (ADR-0007); the tenant, the actor and the causal chain travel as CloudEvents extension attributes, whose names are lower case without separators as the specification requires. Fields may be added; removing or reinterpreting one requires a .v2 delivered alongside .v1 for at least two minor releases (domain-model.md §4).

id.description: UUIDv7. Stable across delivery attempts, so a consumer deduplicates on it (at-least-once delivery).

source.description: The installation and the bounded context that produced the event.

subject.description: What the event is about, so that a consumer can filter without parsing the payload.

actorid.description: Absent when the system itself acts. No label: an event leaves the installation, and a name is personal data a subscriber does not need in order to react (ADR-0018).

onbehalfof.description: The principal an automation rule or an agent runs as.

correlationid.description: Everything that came out of one original action carries the same value. A root event is its own correlation.

causationid.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for an action a person took.

causationdepth.description: Distance from the original action. The rule engine stops at 5 and marks the run ABORTED_LOOP (automation.md §2).

data.description: The reference rather than a snapshot of the entry, for the reason the label events give: a set is not a field, and an entry snapshot would have to carry the whole set to be useful. The media object is not in it either - its record is read through GET /media/{mediaId}, and an event carrying a download target would be handing out a capability to every subscriber.

collection_id.description: The collection the entry belongs to, which is where the permission to see the attachment is resolved from.

media_id.description: The media object that was attached. What a rule reacts to, and what the media garbage collection counts.
